title: Planetary Nebula Sh2-174
caption: The planetary nebula Sh2-174, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: A very blue star sits near the center of a patch of blue gas in this wide-field view. This is Sh2-174 in the constellation Cepheus, an unusual and ancient planetary nebula.

A planetary nebula forms when a star of low mass sheds its outer layers as it dies. What remains of the star's core is a white dwarf, and normally it lies very close to the middle of the cloud it has cast off.

Sh2-174 breaks that pattern. Its white dwarf, the very blue star, is shifted off to the right rather than sitting at the center. Astronomers put this lopsidedness down to the nebula running into the thin interstellar gas that surrounds it. A planetary nebula normally expands evenly around its star, so an off-center white dwarf is a clue that something outside the nebula is at work.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope combined broadband and narrowband filters. B is shown in blue, I in orange, hydrogen-alpha in red and oxygen [O III] in blue.
